messages:
sam: Customer onboards Private control plane in prod VPC; their agent is failing to complete mTLS to our control plane. They report 'handshake failure' and 502 errors.
maria: Thanks — can you paste the immediate error from their agent logs?
sam: Here:

  2026-10-05T09:12:03Z error grpc: failed to create secure client: tls: handshake failure
  mTLS: client cert provided, server did not respond with ServerHello

josh: Quick checks: are they hitting the right hostname (control-api.redwood-private.example) and not an internal load balancer? Also confirm SNI is present.
karen: Asked customer to run:

  openssl s_client -connect control-api-redwood-private.example:443 -servername control-api-redwood-private.example -cert client.pem -key client.key -tlsextdebug -status

sam: Customer pasted output (sanitized):

  CONNECTED(00000003)
  TLS server name: control-api.redwood-private.example
  Certificate chain
   0 s:CN = control.redwood.local
     i:CN = Redwood-Private-Root
  ---
  New, TLSv1.3, Cipher is TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
  (No ServerHello was printed after ClientHello)
  SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to control-api.redwood-private.example:443
  ---
  140736192193856:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1557:SSL alert number 40

maria: hmmm. "No ServerHello" but an alert. Could be our edge not receiving ClientHello or upstream dropping because of missing SNI value or L4 firewall. Also corporate NGFW can inject reset when it sees mTLS client certs.

infra-bot: FYI control-plane instance pool healthy, no recent reloads, cert expiry check: control cert valid until 2027-01-12.

josh: Ask them to tcpdump from their egress NAT to see if SYN/ClientHello leaves and whether we reply. Suggested filter:

  sudo tcpdump -i any host control-api.redwood-private.example and port 443 -w /tmp/redwood.pcap

sam: They shared a pcap snippet. Observations:
 - Client sends ClientHello with SNI = control-api.redwood-private.example
 - ClientHello uses TLS 1.3, key_share x25519
 - No ServerHello seen
 - Shortly after, an RST from their corporate firewall (10.10.0.1) to client port

karen: That points to egress block/NAT proxy intervening. Two possibilities: 1) corporate firewall inspects mTLS and rejects, 2) egress allowlist only allows specific FQDN/IP pairs and our control-plane IP fell out of range.

maria: Also check whether they are going through an HTTP proxy that strips TLS client certs. Ask: do they have proxy env vars set (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY)?
sam: Customer replied: no proxy variables, but they have a transparent TLS-inspecting appliance in egress path.

eng-oncall: If there's TLS inspection, mTLS will fail because appliance cannot present the client's cert to our server. We need them to bypass inspection for control plane hosts or permit passthrough for IPs.

josh: Workaround: ask customer to add control-plane IPs to egress allowlist and disable TLS interception for those IPs. Also confirm NAT preserves source port so client cert signature isn't broken.

sam: Also noticed their MTU was set to 1300; not likely culprit but worth noting. Customer applied bypass rule and re-tested.

customer (quoted by sam): After bypass: openssl shows ServerHello and handshake completed. Agent succeeded and control plane registered.

maria: Great. Root cause appears to be the TLS-inspecting appliance (corporate NGFW) resetting mTLS ClientHello because it can't proxy client certificates. Action items:
 - support: document diagnostic steps for customers with TLS inspection (tcpdump openssl s_client, pcap signs)
 - infra: add control-plane IPs to the private deployment onboarding docs with guidance for egress allowlist and TLS passthrough
 - eng-oncall: consider adding a health-check endpoint that uses non-mTLS port for initial probe? (low priority)

karen: I'll open a KB article and escalate docs update. Sam, please confirm when KB is published.
sam: Will do. Closing thread once KB link posted. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: KB created: /kb/private-egress-tls-inspection.md

sam: KB link received, sending to customer. Thread resolved.
